claim_verbatim: Forecasts give this event a 69% shot at beating every El Niño since 1950 on RONI, with a pile of models at or above +3.0°C Niño-3.4.
context: Additional. He is carrying a forecast probability, same treatment as the NOAA 75% he republished.
source: Essay: The 1/1000 Year El Niño Almanac: 2026–2027 Chokepoints
resolution_criterion: YES if the peak relative ONI (RONI) of the 2026-27 El Niño, on the NOAA series, is higher than every El Niño peak since 1950; NO otherwise. The +3.0°C Niño-3.4 clause in the same sentence is model output he reports and is not part of this criterion.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if the peak relative ONI (RONI) of the 2026-27 El Niño, on the NOAA series, is higher than every El Niño peak since 1950; NO otherwise. The +3.0°C Niño-3.4 clause in the same sentence is model output he reports and is not part of this criterion.
resolution_source_planned: NOAA CPC relative ONI / RONI series for the 2026-27 event
mechanism: A Super El Niño on the warmest sea in the satellite record, with eastern-Pacific variability already above the pre-industrial baseline he cites from Cole et al.
consensus_source: Forecast ensemble as cited in the essay (outlooks he dates before the 6 Sep 2026 ABC briefing)
notes: Additional. Stated 69% is the ensemble figure he published, so edge is zero unless he was adding his own number, which the sentence does not. The underlying model table was not re-fetched outside the essay. Event still running.

claim_verbatim: By 2040, Africa will be the only region with a growing working-age population, requiring the creation of 2 million jobs per month to absorb new entrants.
context: Additional to the robotics calls already logged from this essay.
resolution_criterion: YES if the UN World Population Prospects edition current at end-2040 shows Africa as the only UN region whose working-age population is larger than in 2025; the 2 million jobs/month clause is the magnitude test and is right if the UN or ILO figure for jobs required is between 1.5 and 2.5 million per month. NO if another region also has a growing working-age population.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if the UN World Population Prospects edition current at end-2040 shows Africa as the only UN region whose working-age population is larger than in 2025; the 2 million jobs/month clause is the magnitude test and is right if the UN or ILO figure for jobs required is between 1.5 and 2.5 million per month. NO if another region also has a growing working-age population.
resolution_source_planned: UN World Population Prospects; ILO jobs estimates
mechanism: The West and most of Asia age while Africa's working-age population keeps growing, so the global labour gap is either filled by African workers or by AI.
notes: Additional. Reads as a UN-style demographic projection he states in his own voice. No dated consensus probability was retrieved this pass, so none is recorded.

claim_verbatim: By 2024, China controlled more than 45% of global smelting and refining capacity, with projections exceeding 50% by 2040
source: Essay: THE SOVEREIGN COPPER SPREAD AS A SYSTEM
resolution_criterion: YES if ICSG or an equivalent statistical office reports China's share of global copper smelting plus refining capacity above 50% for 2040; NO if the share is 50% or below.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if ICSG or an equivalent statistical office reports China's share of global copper smelting plus refining capacity above 50% for 2040; NO if the share is 50% or below.
resolution_source_planned: ICSG copper smelting and refining capacity
mechanism: Midstream capacity is built for control, not for the smelter's own margin, so Chinese share keeps rising past half.
notes: The 45% by 2024 clause is history, not the forecast. 'Projections' is not in the probability map; mapped to the 'likely' bin 0.70 for Craig to confirm. The sentence does not name whose projection.

claim_verbatim: The West is unintentionally transferring $20–28 billion annually in critical minerals value to China, a loss projected to grow to $150–220 billion over the next decade.
source: Essay: We Need to Build The Pilbara Processing Commons
resolution_criterion: YES if a government, IEA or equivalent estimate of cumulative critical-minerals processing value transferred from Western unprocessed exports to Chinese refining over the ten years from mid-2026 is at least USD 150 billion; NO if a comparable estimate is under USD 150 billion. If no such estimate exists on the due date, leave unresolved rather than false.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if a government, IEA or equivalent estimate of cumulative critical-minerals processing value transferred from Western unprocessed exports to Chinese refining over the ten years from mid-2026 is at least USD 150 billion; NO if a comparable estimate is under USD 150 billion. If no such estimate exists on the due date, leave unresolved rather than false.
resolution_source_planned: IEA critical minerals outlook or an Australian government value-add estimate
mechanism: Exporting unprocessed concentrates hands the refining margin and hitchhiker metals (gallium, scandium, rare earths) to Chinese refiners.
notes: The same band reappears in The Hidden Subsidy (17 Jun 2026) as ten years of a $20–28 billion annual run-rate, and that essay says the decade value could be even higher. The 'could' upside is not a separate scored call. 'Projected' mapped to 0.70.
